subject: MSA: consequential damages carve-out — scope and mutuality
messages:
From: Sienna Forbes <sforbes@acmehealth.com>
To: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com, dlang@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MSA v4 — consequential damages language

Rafael — attaching our redlines (ACME_MSA_v4_redline.docx). We appreciate the work to get this across the finish line. Two callouts from our GC team that we want to put on the table so we don't go back-and-forth later:

1) Consequential/special/incidental/punitive damages — ACME is asking for a one-way carve-out where ACME can recover consequential damages arising from Redwood's breach or gross negligence, while Redwood's recovery against ACME would remain limited to the order form cap.
2) Definition of consequential/special damages — our redline includes a broad definition (including lost profits, lost business, and third-party claims) and an explicit carve-out for downstream clinical impacts (critical for our compliance team).

We know this is a big ask. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept any of the below options (we included them inline in the doc):
- Mutual exclusion of consequential damages (Redwood prefers this)
- One-way exclusion for ACME only (ACME prefers this)
- Mutual exclusion but with clinical-impact carve-out for ACME only (compromise)

Happy to hop on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks —
Sienna Forbes
Sr. Contracts Counsel | Acme Health

Looping legal and account lead. Key points from ACME: they're proposing a one-way consequential damages exception + a broad definition that specifically calls out downstream clinical impacts. They flagged that it's a high priority for their compliance team.

Quick asks:
- Laura: can you review ACME_MSA_v4_redline and advise if we can accept a narrow clinical-impact carve-out while keeping the general exclusion mutual?
- Marissa: from a commercial perspective, is this a deal-breaker if we push back and insist on mutual exclusion? Any guidance on what concession (credits, higher cap, SLA uplift) could move them?
- Neha: if we agree to any carve-out, what evidence/safeguards should we require (limits, indemnity threshold, incident reporting, audit rights)?

I attached our internal liability summary as reference. Timebox: can we aim for a response to ACME by EOD Monday (10/19)? We should avoid letting this sit overnight with legal.

Thanks —

Subject: Re: Fwd: ACME MSA v4 — consequential damages language

Rafael — reviewed ACME's redlines. High-level position:

1) We should keep the consequential/special/incidental/punitive exclusion mutual and narrowly define consequential damages to exclude "indirect" or "foreseeable" loss but explicitly carve in third-party claims and regulatory fines only where caused by Redwood's willful misconduct or gross negligence.

2) Clinical-impact carve-out: we're open to a very tightly scoped carve-out limited to (a) documented clinical misrouting or data corruption that directly causes measurable patient harm attributable to Redwood's software, (b) subject to a separate sub-cap equal to 2x the order-form fees for the preceding 12 months, and (c) conditioned on ACME having followed published integration and safety checklist. No punitive or consequential recoveries beyond that.

3) Evidence/safeguards: incident timeline, root-cause analysis, third-party expert review (if disputed), pre-agreed remediation plan, and a 180-day written notice and mitigation period before third-party litigation for clinical-impact claims.

Rationale: keeps our overall mutual exclusion (market standard), while giving ACME a narrow, defensible path for very specific clinical harms — with caps and procedural safeguards to manage exposure.

If commercial wants to trade credit/discount in exchange for a broader carve-out, propose we tie concession to a higher minimum annual commitment and a 12-month committed term.

I can draft a markup to ACME's doc with the language above if you want.

—Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Sienna Forbes <sforbes@acmehealth.com>

Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com, dlang@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MSA v4 — consequential damages language

Thanks Rafael and Laura — appreciate the quick review. ACME's position:

- We understand Redwood's preference for mutual exclusion. However, because our deployments involve clinical decision workflows, our board requires the ability to recover consequential losses in the event of downstream patient impact.

- Our security/compliance team reviewed Laura's suggested sub-cap and procedure and are generally comfortable, but the business asks whether a one-way exception for clinical-impact claims only (ACME can recover; Redwood remains capped) is possible as a final ask.

We are prepared to: (a) accept the sub-cap and procedural safeguards Laura proposed, (b) add a joint monitoring/notification SLA tied to our go-live acceptance, and (c) agree to a mutual non-punitive clause to limit damages beyond the sub-cap.

If Redwood can consider a one-way carve (clinical-impact only) in exchange for a 12-month committed term + 10% revenue uplift over the proposed order form pricing, that will get final approval from our CFO.

Please let us know if Redwood can entertain the one-way clinical carve with the proposed commercial give.

Sienna
Sr. Contracts Counsel | Acme Health
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Sienna Forbes <sforbes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MSA v4 — consequential damages language

Sienna — thanks for the clarity and the commercial proposal. Next steps from our side:

1) Legal (Laura): please prepare two short redline options we can send to ACME by EOD Tuesday — (A) mutual exclusion with clinical-impact sub-cap and procedural safeguards (Laura's preferred); (B) narrow, one-way clinical-impact carve-out for ACME only, conditioned on (i) 12-month committed term, (ii) 10% uplift on order form pricing, and (iii) the safeguards you proposed. Keep the language tight and avoid broad phrases like "any downstream clinical impacts" — specify the categories and process.

2) Commercial (Marissa): please confirm whether the 10% uplift + 12-month term is feasible from revenue/renewal forecasting perspective. If we accept option B commercially, what's the approval path (VP Sales / RevOps signoff)?

3) Ops (Neha): if we land on either option, list the operational gating items ACME must meet before any clinical carve applies (integration checklist, SOC2/ISO8k evidence, incident triage contact, etc.).

Goal: get ACME to sign by 10/28. If legal can't support option B, we'll present A to ACME and offer a one-time onboarding credit (up to 5% of first-year fees) if they take the 12-month committed term.

I'll coordinate a 30-minute call with ACME and our GC if the redlines don't resolve quickly.

Best —
Rafael Mendes
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
